subject: Stranded burst quota reallocation proposal
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stranded burst quota — proposal to reallocate for Zephyr pilot

Hi team,

We have ~18 GPU slots in the 'pilot-burst' slice that are effectively stranded: the team that reserved them paused their runs last week and the autoscale eviction window doesn't release them until Oct 1. Zephyr Labs (deal HB-3421) is asking for a short-term carve of 12 GPUs for 72 hours to validate production throughput next week.

Ask:
- Approve temporary reallocation of 12 GPUs from pilot-burst -> zephyr-pilot for the window 2026-09-20 00:00 UTC -> 2026-09-23 00:00 UTC.
- Grant an exception to the autoscale eviction policy for that slice for the window and a one-time routing priority bump so their traffic lands on the reserved nodes.

Rationale: this is a low-risk, high-impact move — Zephyr's POC is on a contract path and validating now materially improves conversion. I attached a short usage report and an ROI sketch.

If ops needs a canary plan or a shorter carve, happy to work through it. Wanted to get product + infra alignment before looping in Hana from CS and Anna at Zephyr.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stranded_quota_report.csv (csv), roi_analysis.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stranded burst quota — proposal to reallocate for Zephyr pilot

Lauren —

Thanks for the write-up. A couple quick concerns from capacity fairness and SLA perspectives:

- Can we confirm these 18 slots are fully unused and not needed for any standing internal canaries or nightly jobs? We don't want churn to cause regressions for other pilots.
- If we do a carve, I lean toward carving 8 GPUs first (smaller blast radius) and scaling to 12 only if Zephyr hits their throughput targets in a 6-hour canary.
- Need ops confirmation we can restore the slice to its original state without disrupting other reserved slices.

If product + infra are comfortable with a staged approach and a rollback play, I'm OK to greenlight in principle. Can we make time today for a 30-min sync?

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Lauren Bishop wrote:
> We have ~18 GPU slots in the 'pilot-burst' slice that are effectively stranded...

—Marcus

Marcus Lin
Tech Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stranded burst quota — proposal to reallocate for Zephyr pilot

Team —

Product is supportive of a temporary carve provided we put guardrails in place. Proposed minimum guardrails:

- Staged carve: start with 8 GPUs for a 6-hour canary window, escalate to 12 only after canary success metrics (p99 latency, error rate, token throughput) are met.
- Explicit routing policy: traffic tagged from zephyr-pilot and routed to reserved nodes; no cross-tenant overcommit on those nodes.
- Timeboxed TTL and automated revert at 2026-09-23 00:00 UTC unless an extension is explicitly approved with justification.

If infra can implement the routing flag as a temporary patch, attach it here and ops can run the carve. I've included a small diff of the routing change I propose.

Kimberly Park
Group Product Manager — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_routing_patch.diff
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 14:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Stranded burst quota — proposal to reallocate for Zephyr pilot

We can support a one-time carve with a 72-hour TTL and an automated rollback. Requirements from infra/ops side:

- Canary traffic: push 10% of expected Zephyr traffic to the carve during the first 6 hours to validate routing and warm KV caches. If p99 latency > target or error rate spikes, we automatically scale the carve down and roll traffic back.
- Rollback plan: a single CLI toggle to flip routing back and a scheduled job that reclaims the carved GPUs at the TTL expiration.
- Audit trail: we need an event log and a short post-mortem template to fill after the carve window.

Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-quota-carve
I'll create the carve 24 hours after we have product sign-off and a confirmed canary payload. For fairness, we should also notify any internal teams that have runbooks referencing pilot-burst.

—Dev

Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Cho <anna.cho@zephyr.com>, ml-ops@zephyr.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stranded burst quota — proposal to reallocate for Zephyr pilot

Thanks all — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Plan agreed: staged carve (8 -> 12), 6-hour canary at start, 72-hour TTL, automated rollback at TTL expiry. Dev, please proceed with carve 24 hours after product posts the canary payload (Kimberly, can you share the payload and the exact target metrics?).

I've scheduled a 30-min sync tomorrow 2026-09-17 10:00 AM PT to walk through the runbook and confirm monitoring hooks. Calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/9f3b

Looping Anna at Zephyr to confirm their canary payload and to set expectations on the window.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
